title: SIEM integration blueprint: Splunk / Datadog / Sentinel - customer requirements & connector spec
content:
Purpose:
This working blueprint lists requirements, transport options, schema mappings, security controls, and troubleshooting guidance for shipping SIEM exports (Splunk HEC, Datadog intake, Azure Sentinel) from Redwood Inference. It’s intended for security, SRE, and integrations engineers working with customers to turn on SIEM ingestion for audit/event telemetry and evidence artifacts.

Scope and goals:
- Standardize an NDJSON audit/event export format derived from RBAC v2 + audit-log schema.
- Provide connector deployment options (push webhook/HEC, forwarder, Event Hub/Kafka pull) and configuration templates.
- Surface customer network and security requirements (mTLS, IP allowlists, retention, encryption, PII controls).
- Define field mappings and sample events for Splunk, Datadog, and Sentinel.
- Outline evidence automation flow for attachments/evidence records referenced from audit events.

Supported SIEM targets (initial):
- Splunk (HTTP Event Collector - HEC)
- Datadog (Logs API / intake with JSON payloads)
- Microsoft Sentinel (Log Analytics Data Collector API or Event Hub for high-throughput)

Connector modes (deployment options):
1) Push (recommended for most customers)
   - Redwood pushes NDJSON batches to customer endpoint (HEC / Datadog / Log Analytics HTTP).
   - TLS required; mutual TLS optional (strongly recommended for enterprise).
   - Best for customers that want Redwood-managed delivery and retries.
2) Forwarder / Agent (customer-managed)
   - Redwood publishes to an S3 bucket or customer endpoint; customer forwarder (e.g., Splunk UF, Datadog Agent) pulls and forwards.
   - Good for customers that do not allow inbound traffic or require agent-based integration.
3) Pull (Event Hub / Kafka)
   - Export into a message bus (Azure Event Hub, AWS MSK/Kafka) under customer-owned topic/namespace.
   - Fits high-throughput customers and those with central observability architectures.

Transport and batching rules (applies to Push mode):
- Payload format: Newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON). Each line is a single JSON audit/event object.
- Max batch size: 5 MB uncompressed or 10,000 events, whichever first.
- Max single event size: 256 KB (base64 evidence links excluded).
- Flush interval: 1s or when batch size reached.
- Compression: gzip supported and recommended (Content-Encoding: gzip).
- Retries: exponential backoff (initial 500ms, multiplier 2, max attempts 5).
- Idempotency: each event contains request_id and event_id. For at-least-once semantics, receivers should dedupe on request_id or event_id plus timestamp.
- Ordering: best-effort by tenant/route; no strict global ordering guarantee across multiple worker processes.

Security requirements and recommendations for customers:
- TLS: TLS 1.2+ required. For high-security customers, support mutual TLS (mTLS) and client cert pinning.
- IP allowlist: provide Redwoods push IP ranges when using push mode; for S3/event hub, provide bucket/policy details.
- Auth: HEC token for Splunk, Datadog API key (scoped for logs), Azure SharedKey or Managed Identity for Event Hub/Log Analytics. Tokens should be rotated and scoped.
- Minimum privileges: the integration principal must only have write/log ingestion privileges.
- Time sync: customer endpoint should be NTP-synced to avoid large skew in _time.
- Data residency: specify region for Event Hub/S3 export when required.

RBAC v2 + audit log mapping notes:
- Audit events include explicit RBAC context: role_id, role_name, role_hash, principal_id, principal_type (user/service), principal_roles (list), and policy_snapshot (short hash).
- For every authorize/deny decision include decision_reason and policy_version.
- Recommended audit fields (canonical):
  timestamp: ISO8601 UTC
  tenant_id: customer account id
  project_id: project/route id
  environment: prod/staging
  service: redwood-inference
  event_id: uuidv4
  request_id: correlated request id
  actor_id: user|service id
  actor_role(s): list
  action: e.g., model.generate, model.load, auth.token.create, role.grant
  resource_type: model|route|token|deployment|key
  resource_id: opaque id
  outcome: success|failure|denied
  error_code: optional internal code
  latency_ms: integer
  user_ip: ip address (if applicable)
  user_agent: string
  auth_method: oauth|api_key|mTLS
  policy_hash: short
  request_payload_digest: sha256 hex (only when payloads stored externally)
  evidence_refs: list of evidence artifact references (see evidence automation section)

Field mappings to SIEMs (notes):
- Splunk: use index provided by customer, sourcetype: redwood:audit:json, host: tenant_id, _time parsed from timestamp field. HEC header Authorization: Splunk <token>.
- Datadog: send JSON with ddsource: redwood_inference, service: redwood-inference, tags: [tenant:<tenant_id>,env:<environment>]. Datadog will index top-level attributes; include action, outcome as top-level strings.
- Sentinel: when using Log Analytics Data Collector, use a custom record type RedwoodAudit_CL. Field names should append _s or _d per Azure ingestion rules (e.g., tenant_id_s, latency_ms_d). For Event Hub ingestion, provide a mapping function on the customer side or use Azure Functions to transform.

Sample event (one line NDJSON):
{
  "timestamp": "2025-01-07T21:24:33.123Z",
  "tenant_id": "acct-7b2f9",
  "project_id": "proj-03",
  "environment": "prod",
  "service": "redwood-inference",
  "event_id": "4f1e6bf4-8b2a-4f2a-9d0b-6ea9c4e1a1c3",
  "request_id": "req-8a6b5c",
  "actor_id": "user-182",
  "actor_roles": ["dev","admin"],
  "action": "model.generate",
  "resource_type": "route",
  "resource_id": "route-chat-1",
  "outcome": "success",
  "latency_ms": 143,
  "user_ip": "3.221.17.44",
  "user_agent": "redwood-sdk/1.2.0",
  "auth_method": "api_key",
  "policy_hash": "a1b2c3d4",
  "evidence_refs": ["s3://redwood-evidence/acct-7b2f9/evid-21.json?sig=..."]
}

Evidence automation (how to handle attachments and PII):
- Evidence artifacts (e.g., request/response payloads, AV files) are stored in a long-term object store with tenant-scoped prefix. Audit events reference evidence by signed short-lived URL (default 7 days) and include a request_payload_digest (sha256) to verify integrity.
- For customers that do not accept payloads in their SIEM, Redwood can optionally send only metadata and store payloads in customer-owned S3 (requires cross-account policy).
- PII minimization: redact sensitive fields at point of export when required by customer agreement. Redaction is configurable per-route/policy.

Connector configuration examples (Push mode):
- Splunk HEC (example headers and endpoint):
  Endpoint: https://inbound.mycompany.com:8088/services/collector/event/1.0
  Headers: Authorization: Splunk <HEC-TOKEN>
  Content-Type: application/json
  X-Redwood-Tenant: acct-7b2f9
  Recommended sourcetype: redwood:audit:json

- Datadog Logs API (example):
  Endpoint: https://http-intake.logs.datadoghq.com/v1/input
  Headers: DD-API-KEY: <APIKEY>, Content-Type: application/json
  Add ddsource: redwood_inference and service: redwood-inference to each event.

- Azure Sentinel / Log Analytics (Data Collector API example):
  Endpoint: https://<workspace-id>.ods.opinsights.azure.com/api/logs?api-version=2016-04-01
  Auth: SharedKey <workspaceId>:<signature> or use Azure Managed Identity when pushing to Event Hub owned by customer.
  Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
  Log-Type: RedwoodAudit

Operational SLAs and throughput considerations:
- For push mode, default per-tenant burst limit: 1,000 events/s (subject to contract). For larger customers, recommend dedicated export pipeline (Event Hub or S3 + forwarder).
- Redwood export workers autoscale; customers must provide endpoint that can accept sustained throughput (TLS concurrency).
- Observability: Redwood exposes per-tenant export metrics (success_rate, avg_latency_ms, last_failure) in Console and via Prometheus metrics.

Failure modes and recommended handling (receiver side):
- 429 / rate-limited: Redwood will backoff and retry up to configured attempts; receiver should return Retry-After header when rejecting.
- 5xx: transient; Redwood retries.
- 4xx (bad request / auth failure): treat as configuration error; stop retries until config fixed.
- Duplicate events: receivers should dedupe on event_id or request_id + timestamp window.

Testing checklist before go-live (customer):
- [ ] Provide HEC/Datadog/Azure endpoint and test token.
- [ ] Provide IP allowlist entries or accept Redwood push IP ranges.
- [ ] Confirm TLS and mTLS expectations; share CA cert if using mTLS.
- [ ] Create test index (Splunk) or test workspace (Sentinel) and provide ingestion examples.
- [ ] Validate sample NDJSON events arrive and fields parse correctly (timestamps, tenant_id, action).
- [ ] Verify evidence link fetching/permissions and checksum validation.
- [ ] Agree on retention/PII redaction rules and confirm sample redacted event.

Monitoring and troubleshooting notes:
- Common problems: timestamp parsing (time zones/skew), token misconfiguration, large single events causing HEC rejects, CA trust issues for mTLS.
- Debug steps: check raw HTTP logs on receiver, ingest a single synthetic event with known timestamp, validate JSON schema against schema validator (links above).

Open questions / items for security review (TODOs):
- Decide default evidence signed URL TTL for enterprise vs standard accounts (7 days vs 24 hours).
- Policy for storing redacted vs original payloads for compliance customers.
- Runtime toggles for full-payload vs metadata-only audit exports per route.

Notes on uniqueness: this doc focuses on architecture, field mapping and customer operational checklist (different emphasis from playbooks or connector spec docs). Treat as working blueprint — will iterate with SRE and Integrations.

Owner: Priya Nair (security-and-compliance)
Reviewers: Alex Chen, Diego Martinez, Samira Okafor

Last updated: 2025-01-08
